_note: Lunar reference per base type. The 0-1 values in scores.csv ARE the similarity to the Moon (1 = equal); no 0-1 target values. Moon values are raw, in earth_unit. score_method: target = similarity, counts in SCORE_TOTAL if weight > 0; display = shown, weight 0; rank = no lunar value yet; not computed = no pipeline value yet. A column can mean different things per base type (e.g. DRIVABLE: Polar display share, Mare scored similarity): always read it through targets[BASE_TYPE].

polar.label: Shackleton rim + floor (lunar south pole)
polar.total_rule: score (vs Moon): weighted mean of the axes with in_total = true

criteria.label: 1 Sunny ridge
criteria.limitation: Known limitation: on the Moon 'lit' is the visible fraction of the solar DISC (PGDA AVGVISIB, extended Sun); on Earth it is the Sun's CENTRE above the horizon (point Sun). Both give 0.5 on flat land at the pole; on terrain they can differ where the Sun stays partly hidden for long stretches (disc fraction > 0 while the centre is already below the horizon).

moon.source: PGDA product 69 AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608.TIF (Mazarico et al. 2011, LOLA-modelled, 60 m, hourly over 18.6 yr; visible solar-disc fraction)
moon.zone: floor = bowl pixels < 10 deg connected to the low point; rim = outside the bowl, at most 1 km from its edge (criterion-10 zone)

criteria.label: 4 Grazing sun

criteria.fact: No Earth analog possible: near the lunar equator the surface reaches about 387-397 K at noon and cools to about 95 K just before sunrise, a day-night swing of roughly 290-300 K (LRO Diviner, Williams et al. 2017, Icarus, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.08.012). Earth's largest surface swings are far smaller. Shown for information, weight 0.
